extracted.intended_audience: prospective applicants to the Paul & Daisy Soros Fellowships (New Americans seeking graduate funding)
extracted.subtask_description: Applying for the Paul & Daisy Soros Fellowships, a merit-based graduate funding program that selects 30 New Americans annually to support their graduate education and lifelong community engagement. The fellowship emphasizes personal background as New Americans and applicant qualities like creativity, originality, initiative, and sustained accomplishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: New American eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides merit-based funding for New Americans, immigrants and children of immigrants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program targets 'New Americans' — defined on the page as immigrants and children of immigrants — as the eligible applicant population. (Page emphasizes honoring America’s immigrant experience.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Graduate education focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Each year, we invest in the graduate education of 30 New Americans—immigrants and children of immigrants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowship support is intended to fund graduate-level study; applicants should be pursuing or planning to pursue graduate education. The program selects 30 Fellows each year to receive support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection emphasis: creativity, originality, initiative, and sustained accomplishment
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection is through a free merit-based process that emphasizes creativity, originality, initiative, and sustained accomplishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These four qualities are highlighted as the principal evaluative dimensions — applicants should demonstrate creative thinking, original approaches, initiative in their work or lives, and a record of sustained accomplishment. The page presents these attributes as central to the selection decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential to make significant contributions to US society, culture, or academia
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows are described as 'poised to make significant contributions to US culture, society and academia.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are expected to show evidence or promise of making meaningful contributions in their field, to US society, culture, or academic disciplines. This forward-looking impact/promise is part of how selections are framed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit-based, free application process and cohort size
rubrics_metrics.description: Thirty Paul & Daisy Soros Fellows are selected every year through a free merit-based process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application is free to enter and selection is explicitly merit-based; the program admits a fixed cohort of 30 Fellows annually. Procedural expectations include competitiveness and limited slots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial award amount and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Fellow receives up to $90,000 in financial support over two years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fellowship provides substantial financial support (up to $90,000 total, disbursed over two years), which is intended to empower recipients at critical points in their educations. This is a program feature applicants should note when planning finances and timeframe.
